title: Johnson–Lindenstrauss flattening in distance form
statement:
Let $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$ and let $n \ge 2$ be an integer, and suppose the target dimension $k$ satisfies $k \ge 32\,\log n / \varepsilon^2$. Then for every finite set $V \subseteq \bbr^d$ of at most $n$ points there exists a linear map $f : \bbr^d \to \bbr^k$ such that, for all $u, v \in V$,
\[
  \sqrt{1-\varepsilon}\,\norm{u - v} \;\le\; \norm{f(u) - f(v)} \;\le\; \sqrt{1+\varepsilon}\,\norm{u - v},
\]
where $\norm{\cdot}$ denotes the Euclidean norm.
hypotheses_covered: V a finite subset of ℝ^d
replaced:
Under the same hypotheses as \texttt{johnson\_lindenstrauss}, there exists a linear
map $f : \mathbb{R}^d \to_L \mathbb{R}^k$ such that for all $u, v \in V$,
\[
  \sqrt{1-\varepsilon}\,\|u - v\| \;\le\; \|f(u) - f(v)\| \;\le\;
  \sqrt{1+\varepsilon}\,\|u - v\|.
\]
